title: 纽约联储威廉姆斯表示，强劲的经济前景导致收益率飙升
content:
纽约联储主席约翰·威廉姆斯 (John Williams) 周三表示，近期国债收益率飙升是经济强劲的结果，而不是市场失调的结果。

这位央行政策制定者在接受 CNBC 采访时补充道，他仍在吸收经济数据，但没有承诺是否认为有必要加息。

“我认为我们必须拭目以待，”威廉姆斯在接受 CNBC 的史蒂夫·里斯曼 (Steve Liesman) 采访时表示。 “Squawk Box”采访来自纽约银行位于曼哈顿下城的总部。 “目前还没有明确的迹象表明目前的货币政策是否足以确保我们在未来一两年内将通胀率带回目标，或者是否需要采取进一步行动来做到这一点。”

“最近的[通胀]数据令人鼓舞，但我们不能只关注一两个月。我们必须全面了解并审视我们拥有的所有……不同的信息，”他补充道。

在金融市场，最近最大的新闻是美国国债收益率跃升至多年高点，尤其是在长期国债收益率上，投资者对通胀和经济增长的预期进行定价。

尽管这种情况一直在发生，但交易员提高了对美联储在 9 月 15 日至 16 日会议上加息的预期，根据芝商所的统计，周三上午的可能性约为 66%。

尽管投资者担心通胀，但威廉姆斯表示，他认为美国国债市场走势与”这是坚实的经济前景的结果。

“推动这一趋势的因素在很大程度上是......美国经济的强劲以及对人工智能、数据中心和一般技术的大量投资推动的强劲的经济前景，”他说。 “因此，我认为这并不是金融状况对经济的影响。更重要的是经济对金融状况的影响。”

威廉姆斯补充道，尽管今年与关税和伊朗战争相关的物价上涨，但他认为通胀预期“稳定”。

作为纽约联储主席，威廉姆斯是负责制定利率的联邦公开市场委员会的永久选民。

title: 荷兰将数十亿黄金运往伦敦以应对“危机准备”
content: Image source,ReutersImage caption,While much of the gold was sold in New York and then repurchased in London, more than 27 tonnes was physically moved to the UKByHenry MoorePublished4 hours agoThe Dutch central bank (DNB) has confirmed that billions of dollars in gold has been taken out of north America and relocated to London, citing "increasing geopolitical unrest".DNB said on Wednesday that 86 tonnes of gold had been removed来自美国和加拿大的复杂行动历时数月。 It is now being held by the Bank of England, where the precious metal can be traded more easily "in a crisis situation".Bank president Olaf Sleijpen said the move was "necessary to strengthen our resilience and preparedness".The decision comes amid an ongoing trade dispute between the US and Canada, withboth countries announcing fresh tariffson each other after failed trade talks.DNB said the transfer, which took place between March and August, saw 27 tonnes of gold bars moved from New York and Ottawa to Zeist in the Netherlands.A similar quantity and quality was then moved to London, with no need to melt the bars down.Exactlyhowso much gold was transported across the Atlantic Ocean has not been revealed.The rest of the transfer was carried out by selling the gold in New York, and repurchasing it in London,the bank said,external."Combining the processes of buying and selling and physical transport has allowed DNB to spread the risks associated with such a complex physical gold relocation," the statement said.DNB did not confirm what it was referring to with its mention of "geopolitical unrest" but the US economy remains in an uncertain position due to the country's ongoing war with Iran, which has impacted global trade.Canada, meanwhile, has been hit hard by US tariffs on its key sectors of steel, aluminium, lumber and automobiles as well as an additional 50% levy on about C$28bn ($20bn; Â£15bn) of Canadian goods announced in August.DNB said that gold that is held with the Bank of England "is regarded as the world's most easily tradable gold," and therefore more readily available in a crisis than if it was still in the US or Canada.Prior to Wednesday's announcement, the DNB held 31.3% of its gold in New York and 19.7% in Ottawa. This has now fallen to 18.5% in both countries.The total Dutch gold stock was 612.4 tonnes at the end of 2025 and has been valued at â¬72.2 billion, DNB said.The bank's share of gold in London has increased from 18.1% to 32.1% after the move, while it still holds 30.8% of its reserves in the Netherlands.Related topicsLondonGoldCanadaUnited StatesTrump tariffsMore on this storyThe US-Canada trade war in 5 chartsPublished2 days agoIran says US strike killed four at wedding in 'war crime' as US denies targeting civiliansPublished6 hours agoAI gold rush draws crypto firms away from BitcoinPublished7 days ago

title: Trump floats renaming Strait of Hormuz the 'Trump Strait'
content:
PresidentDonald Trumpon Wednesday floated renaming theStrait of Hormuz— the central point of contention in the ongoing war againstIranthat the U.S. and Israel started — after himself.

The proposal via a Truth Social post came less than a week after Trump, who is locked in an intensifying feud with Canada, signed an executive order tochange the name of Lake Ontarioto "Lake America."

"Now that we have it under U.S.A. control, should we change the name Hormuz Strait to TRUMP STRAIT???" Trump wrote in thepostWednesday morning.

"Like America itself, it would be 'hotter' than ever before! Thank you for your attention to this matter. President DONALD J. TRUMP," he wrote.

It was not immediately clear how the president would attempt to implement a name change in the strait, which is not near the U.S. The order renaming Lake Ontario directed Interior SecretaryDoug Burgumand his department to update the Geographic Names Information System with the new name. Canada rejected the change, though Google and Apple have recently updated their maps. Early in his second presidential term, Trump also declared he was renaming the Gulf of Mexico as the Gulf of America, a change also rejected by Mexico and other international counterparts. The U.S. borders Lake Ontario and the Gulf of Mexico, both of which have had their names for centuries.

Trump and his administration have repeatedly insisted that Iran has lost control over the strait, which carried one-fifth of the world's oil trade before the war began in late February.

But transits through the waterway remain far below prewar levels, and ship-trackers say they havedropped further in recent days, as military strikes in the region haveresumedfollowing a weekslong hiatus.

The Trump administration asserts that total oil exports from the region are now higher than they were before the war began, if the tally includes Saudi Arabia's and the United Arab Emirate's pipelines that bypass Hormuz.

U.S. Energy Secretary Chris Wright told CNBC on Wednesday that more than 17 million barrels of oil transited the strait on Monday, a new wartime record. Around 20 million barrels per day of crude and products passed through the strait before the war started on Feb. 28.

title: 西南航空将在四个城市开设机场休息室，未来还会有更多
content:
西南航空周三公布了其机场休息室网络的计划，该计划几个月来一直在暗示。

该航空公司表示，其第一批休息室将在德克萨斯州奥斯汀首次亮相；巴尔的摩；檀香山；和田纳西州纳什维尔。该公司表示，这些机场的建设工作已经开始，预计将于 2027 年底开放这些地点。

该航空公司正在与大通银行合作开展这项工作，并表示希望以该公司的 Sapphire Reserve 休息室网络为基础。

“我们的休息室将是这种体验的自然延伸，为乘客提供一个以新方式放松和体验西南航空品牌的场所，”西南航空执行副总裁托尼·罗奇 (Tony Roach) 在一份声明中表示。 “休息室网络的推出代表了对 Rapid Rewards 的战略投资，并加深了我们与大通银行 30 年的合作关系。”

该航空公司表示，客户可以使用大通银行将发行的新的优质西南快速奖励信用卡进入其休息室。该公司表示，该卡将于明年推出，但没有提供任何有关费用的更多细节。

西南航空表示，计划在未来几年内“在高需求的商务和休闲市场”再开设 7 个休息室。

首席执行官鲍勃·乔丹 (Bob Jordan) 几个月来一直在谈论该航空公司进入休息室的问题，他在 12 月告诉 CNBC，它正在“积极寻求”建立一个位置网络的可能性。

“我认为休息室乔丹当时表示，这对我们的客户来说将是一个巨大的下一个好处。

西南航空采取这一举措之际，从达美航空到捷蓝航空的航空公司以及美国运通、第一资本和大通等信用卡公司一直在建设机场休息室，以吸引和留住高消费消费者。

西南航空比任何其他航空公司承载更多的国内客户，在过去一年半中彻底改变了其商业模式。随着激进分子埃利奥特投资管理公司(Elliott Investment Management)的压力加大，它放弃了著名的开放座位，转而采用指定座位，并开始向顾客收取托运行李费用，以增加收入。

title: Lords call for AI 'kill switch' powers in UK
content: 图片来源，Getty Images作者：Zoe Kleinman技术与人工智能编辑2小时前发布一群同行呼吁英国政府在该技术对国家安全构成威胁的情况下能够停用强大的人工智能系统并关闭该国的数据中心。该组织由自由民主党勋爵蒂姆·克莱门特·琼斯领导，他提出了这项措施，作为《网络安全和弹性法案》的修正案，该法案目前正在制定他表示，这将有助于建立一个“重要的安全网”，并提供一种民主负责的手段，“在失控的系统损害我们关键的国家基础设施之前阻止它”。他补充说，该工具只会被用作最后手段。这是本周辩论的同一法案的 65 项修正案之一。另外，9 月 8 日，工党议员 Alex Sobel 计划在名为 ControlAI 的运动团体的支持下，在议会提出一项人工智能安全法案。如果成功，该法案将使英国成为第一个引入立法的七国集团国家，有效阻止超级智能人工智能的发展。最终，这两项提案都需要政府批准才能取得进展。美国立法者还在考虑一项《人工智能杀戮开关法案》。最近几周，人们对人工智能对网络安全的影响进行了越来越多的审查。7月，一组正在接受OpenAI测试的人工智能代理能够逃离他们的测试空间，使用隐藏的留言板进行交流，并侵入另一家科技公司。 Anthropic 限制对其网络工具 Mythos 的访问，理由是它太强大了，不会落入坏人之手。上周，100 家美国科技公司签署了一封联合公开信，警告全球各国政府和组织有关人工智能构成的日益严重的网络威胁，称“改善的窗口正在关闭”。英国长期弹性中心上周发布的外部报告指出，发生了数百起人工智能工具无视指令、逃避保障措施和欺骗的事件。报告称，自 3 月份发布的上一份报告以来，“失控”事件有所增加，并呼吁政府引入紧急权力来管理此类事件。OpenAI 模型失控后，立法者推动人工智能“终止开关”。7 月 23 日发布，顶级科技公司警告网络安全的时间已经不多了。5 天前发布警告射击或宣传噱头 - 我们应该对 OpenAI 黑客攻击有多担心？7 月 25 日发布，订阅我们的技术解码时事通讯关注世界顶级科技故事和趋势。在英国以外？在此注册。相关主题网络安全人工智能自由民主党上议院

title: Faisal Islam: Why bond market wildfire is keeping world leaders up at night
content: Image source,EPA/ShutterstockByFaisal IslamEconomics editorPublished3 hours agoIt is not just the wildfire burning in the bond markets, with many countries facing interest rates at multi-decade highs.The markets lending money to governments appear to be changing more fundamentally too.Over summer, the message has been made clear: countries will have to pay more to borrow cash.The immediate reason is the ongoing closure of the Strait of Hormuz and renewed hostilities between the US and Iran, which has pushed up inflation and, in turn, raised expectations of higher interest rates in the world's major economies.Markets had assumed tensions would subside, and so too would oil and gas prices, ahead of the US midterm elections in November.It was wishful thinking, based on the hope that US President Donald Trump would want the conflict in the Middle East resolved well before Americans go to the polls.But that has not happened, leaving markets pricing in higher energy prices, a chronic Gulf crisis, higher inflation for longer -and so higher interest rates.But that is only part of the story.The bigger picture is rising demand for borrowing across the world - and not just from governments. Big tech companies are turning to the same bond markets to raise hundreds of billions of dollars for investments in AI data centres.Over $219bn (Â£162bn) of debt has already been issued this year by the US "hyperscalers" such as Google, Amazon and Meta, nearly a third of it in currencies other than the dollar, including sterling.The total issued last year was $93bn, while before that it averaged less than $40bn a year. Some expect the tech giants to raise $400-$500bn from the bond markets this year. These are staggering sums, raising competition in the market and pushing up the price for governments.Looking east, there is another major borrower: Japan.It has the highest debt burden, relative to its GDP, of the major economies and is the biggest single lender to the US government. Until recently its central bank's interest rate was zero, but that has crept up to help combat rising inflation.As a result, its government bond yields have been pushed to 30-year highs. Thedeclining value of the yencomplicates things, but the bottom line is that there is a change afoot in the global flow of money.Why are UK borrowing costs rising and what does it mean for me?Published5 hours agoThe biggest factor pushing up rates is the credibility of the borrowing plans set out by major countries. The increase is not based on fears about countries "going bankrupt".But it is based on the brutal market equation that if a country wants to borrow more, and to do so without a credible plan, especially if there are doubts over the stability of a given government, it should expect to pay a higher rate.Influential economists lean on different factors. Mohamed el-Erian told me the AI competition in bond markets was the biggest new factor.Lord Jim O'Neill, says the recent action has been caused by uncertainty about US policy, and in particular efforts by the US Government to try to manage down surging yields.This brings us to the UK. The profound and rolling instability of multiple prime ministers, chancellors, policy U-turns and the seeming inability to push through major structural change in this country over the past decades, has attracted a premium.It was part of Sir Keir Starmer's strategy to try to take on boring reforms and offer markets stability in a bid to lower borrowing costs.It was a shock to many in the markets that despite a landslide majority, Labour could not push through plans to cut Britain's welfare bill. This added to the ups and downs in the gilt markets - the trade in British government debt.Actually, there are signs of green shoots in the underlying economy. Economic growth has been faster than peers so far in 2026, despite the energy price spike.Measures of consumer confidence have ticked back up again. The PM is hoping to build on these signs to help rebuild the economy.But the ongoing rout in global bond markets raises serious questions about the coherence and detail of Burnham's broader plans."More public control" and more support for those struggling with the cost of living sounds like a plan for more spending, while the former could turn off potential investors looking at the country.Burnham's former economic adviser, Lord O'Neill, told me yesterday that the PM's 10-year plan, expected in November, needs to set out how he will tackle "excessive spending".Lord O'Neill believes showing investors he can be decisive on the state pension or the welfare bill will give him breathing room to focus on his favoured infrastructure investments.As interest rates tick up, the trade offs facing the prime minister only get more difficult.Related topicsUK economyUS economyJapanInflationMore on this storyGovernment borrowing, bonds and yields explainedPublished14 February 2025UK long-term borrowing costs highest since 1998 ahead of October BudgetPublished15 hours ago

title: G20 实时更新：卢特尼克告诉 CNBC，白宫准备对半导体征收关税
content:
Artificial intelligenceis taking center stage at theG20gatherings this week.

NvidiaCEO Jensen Huang,AnthropicCo-Founder Tom Brown andOpenAICEO Sam Altman highlight the tech-focused guests on Wednesday for day 2 of the G20 Innovation Ministerial in Chapel Hill, North Carolina.

Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick and White House Office of Science and Technology Policy Director Michael Kratsios are leading the conference, which gathers representatives of theG20 nations, including China, Brazil, Canada, Germany and others.

MetaCEOMark ZuckerbergandTesla/SpaceXCEOElon Muskwere among the tech titans at Tuesday's session.

Lutnick claimed to CNBC that Trump's reanimated tariff policies will usher in a wave of economic benefits, including raising domestic growth, shrinking budget deficits and tamping downspiking bond yields.

He spoke as the 10-year U.S. Treasury yield hit its highest level since November, 2023 amid a global bond sell-off.

U.S. tariff rates under Trump are already highly above historical averages, even after the Supreme Court's February ruling that struck down Trump's expansive "reciprocal" duties.

Lutnick blamed muted U.S. GDP in the second quarter on the high court's ruling, telling "Squawk Box," "Those tariffs came down, imports came flooding in."

After the tariff collapse, "imports come flying in, starting February all the way through the next quarter," resulting in a 1.6% reduction U.S. GDP, he said.

"Over the next couple of weeks, they'll be all back in place, and you'll see imports start to fall, and you'll see GDP rise."

He went on to claim that as Trump finds ways to reimpose the scrapped tariffs, the import taxes will bring in revenues as high as $400 billion a year, reducing America's rapidly increasing budget deficits.

"You're going to see the economy start to kick up again as we go back to above 3 percent and the growth rate and the reduction in the deficit will not only stabilize the bond market, will bring rates down," Lutnick said.

Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang called AI "the great equalizer' and said the technology will democratize intelligence.

"Artificial intelligence will democratize intelligence and capabilities for the G20 countries," Huang said in a fireside chat with Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick. "For the countries that invest in it, it'll help elevate your society, elevate your industry much, much more quickly than you possibly could have imagined before."

Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick doesn't believe the recent rise in Treasury yields is anything to be concerned about.

In an interview with CNBC's "Squawk Box" on Wednesday, Lutnick said he thinks that a pickup in the growth rate of the U.S. economy, as well as a reduction in the deficit — which reached itshighest monthly level in more than five yearsin July — will ultimately "bring rates down."

"I'm comfortable with where things are," he said. "I think what you'll see is rates stabilize and start to decline over the coming, let's say, six months."

On Wednesday, the10-year U.S. Treasurynote yield hit itshighest level since November 2023.

Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick told CNBC that the Trump administration is working on a tariff framework for chips and all the companies know they are coming.

Lutnick confirmed aPoliticoreport from last week that the White House was weighing the move.

"I think what you're going to see is targeted, thoughtful tariff policy that basically says if you build here, you don't pay, but if you don't build here, expect to pay to enter the greatest market in the world," Lutnick said.

The tariffs on semiconductors have been in the works for some time, but the administration hasn't discussed what is being considered publicly.

"We will be successful in semiconductors. They're going to be built in America," he said.

Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick doubled down on blaming Canada amid an ongoing he said-she said over which country is responsible for tanking a trade deal at the 11th hour.

Lutnick told CNBC's "Squawk Box" that Canadian negotiators started "adding crazy ideas to the mix" just hours before a deadline to reach a deal that would avert Trump's 50% tariffs on Canadian goods from taking effect. He pointed to medium- and heavy-trucks for Canada's ask on the Friday the talks devolved.

"And I said to one of the ministers, 'Are you actually trying to blow this up?' And his answer to me was, 'I'm not allowed to say that,'" Lutnick said.

"They blew it up for political reasons only," he said.

Lutnick also allowed that the U.S. may have made last-minute asks, as Trump has said sounds like something he may have done.

Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said the conversation around AI and data centers needs "a big reset," blaming AI companies for doing a terrible job of being trustworthy messengers for the tech boom.

"I think that the AI companies, whether it is the builders of the data centers, whether it is the labs themselves, have done a horrendous job, horrendous job of explaining themselves to the American people," Bessent said in comments Tuesday following the G20 meetings with finance ministers and central bankers in Asheville, North Carolina.

Bessent said the companies need to convince the American people that "all the benefits will not accrue to a small group" and will instead be spread evenly.

Elon Musk, the CEO ofTeslaandSpaceX, said Tuesday that governments should seek to "make things default legal, not default illegal" to help foster growth, likening new companies to saplings in a forest.

"What most countries tend to do is they tend to provide too much support to the large existing trees in the forest, and not enough to the small saplings," he said, adding that the regulatory environment "should be generally biased towards supporting" the small trees.

Musk, the world's richest person, also made several bold predictions on the potential for AI growth and robotics.

"AI will probably increase the global economy by 20% to 30%" he said, adding that in 10 years he expects over a billion humanoid robots out in the world.

Former White House AI czar David Sacks addressed blowback against the AI data center buildout on Tuesday and said local communities can benefit from the construction projects.

"Data centers, if done right, they bring electricity costs down, not up, because the AI companies will generate net new power generation," he said. "That's really the key."

Sacks, a venture capitalist who is co-chair of the President's Council of Advisors on Science & Technology, said if the companies are allowed to generate their own power, then excess can be sent back to the grid, bringing costs down. He also said companies can help pay for grid upgrades.

President Donald Trumpon Monday blasted opposition to data centers, posting on Truth Social that any locale stonewalling the buildout must "want to end up being backwards and poor."

Sacks insisted that it's still a local decision.

"The federal government should not preempt the decision of states with respect to data centers," he said. "It is fundamentally a local decision, and we respect that and have done nothing to change that."

title: 伯克希尔首席执行官格雷格·阿贝尔 (Greg Abel) 告诉 CNBC，数据中心建设面临“更多阻力”
content:
伯克希尔哈撒韦公司首席执行官格雷格·阿贝尔 (Greg Abel) 在周三上午接受 CNBC 的贝基·奎克 (Becky Quick) 采访时指出，美国各地对数据中心建设的抵制越来越大。

阿贝尔表示，“美国各地的社区存在更多的抵制，”阿贝尔表示。

伯克希尔哈撒韦公司对正在进行的计算设施建设的兴趣主要与这些站点的电力和发电有关，阿贝尔评论道，并指出该集团希望与超级计算公司开展业务，只要他们控制成本。

他说：“我们有兴趣为这些超级计算公司提供服务……如果对我们其他客户的费率没有影响的话。”

华尔街的投资者和分析师赞同阿贝尔的评论，指出对可能消耗当地自然资源的大型计算建设项目的有组织的政治抵制日益增加。

纽约州已颁布暂停数据保护令中心建设，而许多其他州则有不同程度的禁令和限制。美国大约有 4,700 个数据中心，而且这个数字还在不断增长。

瑞穗分析师在周二给客户的一份报告中表示，投资者认为数据中心可能是中期选举中的一个重大问题。

“这显然是一个不断变化的情况，因为一些投资者质疑即将到来的中期选举的设置以及围绕资源消耗和有限的长期就业创造的主张的有效性，”瑞穗的 Vikram Malhotra 写道。星期二。

title: 伯克希尔首席执行官阿贝尔表示，Alphabet 在第二季度增持股份后成为人工智能领域的“重要参与者”
content:
伯克希尔·哈撒韦公司首席执行官格雷格·阿贝尔周三与 CNBC 的 Becky Quick 讨论了该集团对谷歌母公司 Alphabet 的巨额投资，称这家科技巨头是人工智能领域的“重要参与者”。

阿贝尔表示，伯克希尔哈撒韦公司清楚地了解人工智能对其公司投资组合的影响，并且谷歌相对于新兴技术的地位很强。

“我们从内部拥有很多可见性他告诉 Quick，伯克希尔哈撒韦公司 15 个月前以 6.5% 的折扣购买了 100 亿美元的 Google 股份。

“他们没有设定规模，但建议我们考虑 100 亿美元。沃伦和我讨论了折扣规模，我建议 6.5% 的折扣，我们对此感到满意，”阿贝尔说。 “然后最终完成了交易。”

根据该公司 8 月份向美国证券交易委员会提交的第二季度投资组合快照，伯克希尔在第二季度总共增持了 170 亿美元的 Alphabet 股票，使其成为伯克希尔哈撒韦股票投资组合中的第三大持股。

截至该公司上次提交的文件，伯克希尔拥有约 1.06 亿股 Alphabet 的 A 类和 C 类股票，目前价值约366亿美元。 Alphabet 的收购是伯克希尔本季度投资组合中最大的一笔收购，但伯克希尔也对达美航空下了重注，将其头寸增加了 44%，即约 16 亿美元。

谷歌是五家所谓的超大规模企业之一，它们执行巨额资本支出，以扩展其运行人工智能的计算能力，另外还有微软、Meta、亚马逊和甲骨文。据投资银行高盛称，2026 年全球超大规模资本支出预计约为 1 万亿美元，但预测之间存在显着差异。

“估计表明，人们普遍引用的超大规模资本支出预测为 7940 亿美元，可能低估了全球人工智能资本支出总额约 2000 亿美元。同时，7940 亿美元的数字可能高估了美国人工智能投资额 200 美元高盛研究人员在 8 月份的分析中写道。

投资者面临的问题是，这些巨额投资将在多大程度上以及在多长时间内获得回报。

人工智能计算工作负载通常分为基于大型数据集和推理或查询响应的算法训练两类。

“随着资本支出和研发在广泛货币化之前继续部署，长期的训练主导阶段会延长投资回报率时间线。”高盛研究人员在五月写道。

title: Private payrolls rose by 38,000 in August, fewer than expected, ADP reports
content:
Private U.S. companies added jobs at a slightly slower-than-expected pace in August, with gains concentrated heavily in health care and a few other industries, ADP reported Wednesday.

The payrolls processing firm said firms added 38,000 workers, fewer than the upwardly revised 46,000 in July and below the Dow Jones consensus estimate for 47,000.

Though job creation held positive, August was the smallest gain since January and reflective of a broader slowdown in the labor market. Moreover, most of the jobs came from three sectors, with multiple others showing declines.

Education and health services added 45,000 to lead all categories, with the latter group being at the forefront of employment growth.

Leisure and hospitality added 16,000 positions an construction was up 12,000. Outside of that, though, there were few growth areas.

Manufacturing lost 17,000 jobs, professional and business services was off 16,000 and both the natural resources and mining as well as trade, transportation and utilities reported declines of 5,000.

Almost all of the gains came from big business, with companies employing 500 or more workers adding 34,000 while those with fewer than 50 employees rose by 3,000.

ADP's numbers also showed that pay gains held steady for the month. The firm added a feature in August in which it broke down growth between base and gross pay, the latter including tips, commissions, bonuses and other earnings.

For those staying in their jobs, base pay rose 3% from a year ago while gross pay increased 4.4%, both unchanged from July. For all workers, the respective increases were 3.2% and 4.7%.

The ADP report serves as a precursor to the Bureau of Labor Statistics' nonfarm payrolls release, due out Friday, which is expected to show an increase of 53,000, after the 23,000 decline in July. The unemployment rate is forecast to hold at 4.1%.

title: 加拿大央行在准备利率决定时考虑特朗普关税冲击
content:
由于与美国的贸易谈判破裂后的报复性关税闪电战，加拿大央行的工作因增长疲弱和通胀上升的前景而变得复杂。

预计这一影响也将指导加拿大央行，加拿大央行将于美国东部时间周三上午 9:45 发布关于加拿大利率的最新决定。

唐纳德·特朗普总统对美国发起新的贸易战”第二大贸易伙伴对加拿大的多种商品征收 50% 的关税。加拿大已宣布报复性关税，将于 9 月 8 日生效，影响超过 200 亿美元的商品。

美国银行经济学家卡洛斯·卡皮斯特兰 (Carlos Capistran) 在周二的一份报告中援引加拿大央行之前的说法写道：“我们预计加拿大央行将保持谨慎态度，重申不确定性很高，并将‘继续评估加拿大经济实力和通胀前景，并准备根据需要调整货币政策’”

“随着与美国的贸易战刚刚升级，贸易不确定性上升，这可能会拖累经济增长，核心通胀处于2%的目标。我们预计关税对通胀只会产生直接影响，不会产生第二轮影响。”

加拿大央行7月份连续第六次决定将基准利率维持在2.25%不变，低于近期峰值5%。加拿大经济第二季度增长了 0.8%，较今年前三个月的 0.1% 有所增长。

同时，最新数据显示，7 月份总体消费者通胀率同比加速至 3%，高于 6 月份的 2.8%，促使交易员预计加拿大央行将在未来 12 个月内加息三次。 但美国银行预计加拿大央行将在未来几个月维持利率不变。

Capistran 表示：“第二季度走强和整体通胀高于目标值得谨慎，但我们认为，与美国的贸易战升级对货币政策来说是更重要的发展。”

高盛预测，由于特朗普的关税。

该银行在 8 月 28 日的一份报告中写道，“这些下行增长担忧和贸易紧张局势的持续波动可能会让加拿大央行在可预见的未来按兵不动。”

title: 随着通胀担忧加剧，全球债券崩盘步伐加快
content:
周三全球政府债券遭到抛售，导致借贷成本进一步飙升。

作为欧元区基准的德国 10 年期国债收益率周三上午上涨 4 个基点，至 3.375%，为 2011 年以来的最高水平。日本 10 年期国债收益率为 3.016%，此前曾突破 3%。周二，这是三十年来的首次。

10年期国债收益率保持在4.8%以上，上次触及这一水平是在2025年初，当时英国10年期国债将其2008年后的高点升至5.25%。

收益率走势与价格相反。

投资者对通胀压力的复苏感到不安，特别是中东新一波冲突推高了油价。这加剧了人们长期以来对美国、日本和法国等主要经济体的财政状况和高债务负担的担忧。

与此同时，世界各地的央行都在为本月的一系列加息做准备，这对债券来说通常是坏消息。美联储主席凯文·沃什(Kevin Warsh)上周在杰克逊霍尔(Jackson Hole)备受关注的讲话中语气强硬，而日本央行预计可能加息以支撑日元贬值，而周二欧盟通胀数据公布后，市场已完全消化欧洲央行加息的预期。

股市也进入避险模式，美国主要股指连续三个交易日下跌，欧洲和亚洲市场也出现亏损。在此之前，尽管地缘政治背景不稳定，但随着对人工智能热潮的热情持续，许多股市今年仍创下了历史新高。

“（市场）的基本原则比以往更加不稳定，”信安资产管理公司首席投资官兼全球股票主管乔治·马里斯周三对 CNBC 的“Squawk Box Europe”节目表示。

“如果资金成本、风险成本上升，这就是你所看到的全球各地收益率上升的情况。”

“你会看到世界各地的债务水平都处于高位，而且还在不断增加。解决这个问题的解决方案似乎并不明显......我认为这是一个问题，”马里斯补充道。

“我认为这一切都发生在全球经济健康增长的时期，你会看到债务水平上升，这意味着如果出现干扰，我们就会处于更加危险的境地。”

title: 石油巨头英国石油公司 (BP) 在董事会发生剧变后完成了主席人选
content:
英国BP周三正式任命伊恩·泰勒(Ian Tyler)为董事长，此前他的前任阿尔伯特·马尼福德(Albert Manifold)出人意料地被解职，导致这家石油巨头的领导层发生剧变。

泰勒于去年4月作为非执行董事加入该公司董事会，并于5月26日被任命为临时董事长。

BP表示，泰勒曾与超过15位首席执行官一起工作过。 BP 高级独立董事阿曼达·布兰克 (Amanda Blanc) 在一份声明中表示：“伊恩拥有丰富的经验，为高管团队提供挑战和支持，同时代表股东保持强有力的治理和监督。”该公司还宣布，布兰克不会在 2027 年年度股东大会上竞选连任，一旦继任者确定，布兰克将辞去董事会职务。被任命为她的职位。

泰勒说，他曾要求布兰克留下来，但她告诉他，四年后，现在是计划她离开董事会的适当时机。

“我将领导董事会的发展，确保我们拥有支持公司战略重点和长期价值创造所需的深度、经验和能力，”泰勒说。

“我致力于与股东建立定期和透明的接触，同时继续支持更广泛的利益相关者。”他补充道，泰勒的任命是在 BP 在经过多年的高管更替和战略划分之后寻求稳定公司之际进行的。这家在伦敦上市的石油巨头正在重心转向其核心石油和天然气业务，同时通过简化其投资组合来优先考虑财务纪律。

周三上午，BP 股价上涨约 0.4%。今年迄今为止，该股已上涨约 25%。

5 月，BP 解除了 Manifold 董事长的职务，立即生效。 Manifold 上任仅约七个月，曾面临与治理标准、监督和行为有关的“严重关切”的指控。

这位前主席反驳了这些指控，称他“在没有警告和解释的情况下”被免职，并且他对自己行为的“完全定性”提出质疑。

在连续突然的领导之后，他的解雇引发了人们对 BP 公司治理的质疑。

2023 年，伯纳德·卢尼 (Bernard Looney) 辞去了首席执行官一职，此前该公司表示，他在过去与同事的关系问题上误导了董事会。他的继任者是 Murray Auchincloss，后者在担任该职位不到两年后辞职。

现任首席执行官梅格·奥尼尔 (Meg O'Neill) 于 12 月接任，成为公司六年内的第四位首席执行官。

title: 华尔街连续第三个下跌日后，股票期货几乎没有变化：实时更新
content:
Stock futures were nearly flat early Wednesday after surging bond yields and oil prices led Wall Street lower for a third straight day.

Dow Jones Industrial Average futuresadded 14 points.S&P 500 futureswas marginally lower andNasdaq 100 futuresslipped 0.3%.

In Asia, Japan'sNikkei 225declined 2.80% while the Topix dropped 2.18%.TheKospifell 3.59%, and the small-cap Kosdaq declined 1.49%. Australia's benchmarkS&P/ASX 200was 1.17% lower. Hong Kong'sHang Seng indexwas down 0.96%, while mainland China's CSI 300 slipped 1.25%.

TheDowfell more than 400 points. Technology stocks dragged the market lower, with theNasdaq Compositesliding by around 1%.

West Texas Intermediate oil prices jumpedabove $90 per barrelon Tuesday, marking its highest level since late July, as the U.S.launched more military strikeson Iran, raising concern that the conflict could escalate once more.

TheU.S. 10-year Treasuryyield climbed to itshighest level since early 2025on Tuesday. The 10-year yield's ascent offered the latest sign of a global selloff in the bond market that some investors fear could look similar to the 1997 Asian financial crisis.

"Higher yields are proving to be the stock market's undoing," said Thierry Wizman, global foreign exchange and rates strategist at Macquarie Group. "They force analysts to discount higher earnings more aggressively, thus forcing [price-to-earnings] multiples downward."

Investors will watch for the ADP's private payrolls data for August on Wednesday. Traders will also monitor factory earnings data and the Federal Reserve's Beige Book.

Investors will follow earnings fromHewlett Packard Enterprise,SnowflakeandBroadcomdue after the bell Wednesday.

Oil rose Wednesday, as Mideast tensions continue to escalate after the U.S. carried out its latest round of attacks on Iran, while Tehran reportedly struck back at U.S. allies.

Futures for international benchmarkBrent crudefor November delivery advanced 0.92% at $95.52 a barrel, paring earlier gains. U.S.West Texas Intermediate futuresfor October rose 0.60% to $90.76 per barrel.

"The longer the war with Iran goes on, oil prices will continue to stay elevated and volatile," said Edward Rosenberg, head of ETFs at Strategy Shares. "Sanctions, stalled negotiations, and mixed signals on whether Iran wants the war to end are swinging prices day to day, not just holding them high."

Shares of Japanese beverage makerIto Ensurged more than 8% Wednesday, following its fiscal first-quarterresults, bucking a broader drop in the country's stocks.

The maker of Oi Ocha green tea on Tuesday reported operating profit of 10.2 billion yen ($63.7 million) for the three months from May through July, up 22% from a year earlier. Revenue rose 3.3% to 135.18 billion yen over the same period.

Operating profit came in well above Citi's forecast of 7.7 billion yen. The bank had expected profit to decline on the back of higher raw material and tea leaf costs, as well as expenses related to the company's vending machine business.

Australia's economic growth beat expectations in the second quarter, expanding 2.1% year on year, data released Wednesday showed.

Economists polled by Reuters had estimated growth at 1.8%, while the economy had expanded by 2.5% in the prior quarter.

On a quarter-on-quarter basis, GDP rose 0.4%, also marginally surpassing expectations of 0.3%. The slight growth was driven by private demand and mining exports.

The Australian Bureau of Statistics said in its statement that households continued to behave cautiously, with spending remaining subdued and rising just 0.4%. Households reduced fuel consumption due to elevated prices owed to the Middle East conflict, and cut domestic and international travel.

Mainland China and Hong Kong indexes opened lower as Asian markets saw a broad decline.

Hong Kong'sHang Seng indexwas down 1.09%, while mainland China's CSI 300 dropped nearly 1%.

The declines in Hang Seng were led by basic materials and industrials sectors, down 3.74% and 3.19%, respectively.

Asia-Pacific markets traded lower early Wednesday, amid concerns over elevated oil prices and higher bond yields and escalating Middle East tensions.

Japan'sNikkei 225declined 1.60% while the Topix dropped 1.44%.

TheKospifell 2.87% at open, while the small-cap Kosdaq declined 2.51%.

Australia's benchmarkS&P/ASX 200was 1.09% lower.

Asia-Pacific markets were set to open broadly lower Wednesday, tracking Wall Street losses amid worries over escalating Middle East tensions, elevated oil prices and higher bond yields.

Japan'sNikkei 225was poised to decline, with the Chicago futures contract at 64,845 and its Osaka counterpart last trading at 64,880, compared with the index's previous close of 66,215.34.

Hong KongHang Seng indexfutures were at 25,176, compared with the index's last close of 25,329.73.

Futures for Australia'sS&P/ASX 200last traded at 8,933, while the index closed at 9,066.70.

Tensions between Iran and the U.S. continue to escalate, after the U.S. carried out its latest round of attacks on Iran.

The U.S. Central Command said in aX post, the strikes "follow recent attempted attacks by the IRGC against commercial shipping in the Strait of Hormuz and against American service members."

A tanker was struck by three unknown projectiles while transiting Hormuz on Monday, theU.K. Maritime Trade Operations Centresaid in an incident report

title: 特朗普称美国不会强迫伊朗在新一轮打击后进行谈判
content:
美国总统唐纳德·特朗普表示，他“并不是试图迫使伊朗回到谈判桌上”，因为美国军队周二在美国本土完成了对这个中东国家的新一轮打击。

特朗普在《真相社会》帖子中重申，美国对霍尔木兹海峡拥有“几乎完全控制”，同时补充说，德黑兰的经济正在崩溃。

他说，伊朗只是“上演不可避免的事情”，并问道“伊朗人民什么时候会起来战斗？”

在 X 上的一篇帖子中，美国中央司令部表示，它袭击了伊朗的防空和通信站点以及雷达系统，以报复该国“最近企图袭击”霍尔木兹海峡的商业航运和美国军人。

德黑兰已对美国的袭击作出回应，目标是美国的盟友约旦。约旦武装部队表示，它遭到了来自伊朗境内的导弹袭击。

约旦武装部队发言人 X 日表示，13 枚导弹中有 10 枚被该国防空系统拦截，其中 3 枚落在偏远地区。没有人员伤亡的报道。

巴林内政部也在当地时间周三早些时候发布了“潜在威胁警报”，敦促公民前往最近的安全地点。威胁的性质尚不清楚。

袭击发生后，周三亚洲交易中油价继续上涨，国际基准布伦特原油期货周二上涨 4.5% 至每桶 94.52 美元，而美国西德克萨斯中质原油期货上涨约 5% 至每桶 90.03 美元，达到 7 月 24 日以来的最高水平。

特朗普早些时候称美国最新的罢工“规模大而有力”，并且威胁称，如果德黑兰对他所谓的“非常正当的袭击”进行报复，伊朗军队将采取进一步军事行动。

美国军队前一天袭击了伊朗拉拉克岛的火箭发射器，伊朗军队周一袭击了美国在约旦的基地。华盛顿声称发射器正准备向海峡发射携带水雷的火箭。

周日的袭击是美国和伊朗在大约一个月内首次进行攻击，此前特朗普政府表示将对德黑兰的支持者发动“经济诺曼底登陆”。

title: 消费者组织称，唐宁街10号的假房源暴露了Booking.com“不合格”
content: Image source,ReutersByLiv McMahonTechnology reporterPublished2 hours agoConsumer group Which? says it was able to create a fake listing for 10 Downing Street on travel giant Booking.com.The UK watchdog said its researchers were able to book a bogus stay at the prime minister's address - as well as leave a fake review noting "hanging out" with resident mouser Larry the cat as a highlight.It said despite clear signs it was fake, Booking.com did not remove the listing until two months after it was uploaded."This limited test is not a true reflection of the experience of millions of listings or reviews published on our platform," a Booking.com spokesperson told the BBC.They said because Which?'s listing was not "live" on its site across the two months it was present, "some of our automatic fraud controls were not triggered to completely remove the closed listing".People could only see the listing and request to book the property during a 20-minute window opened by Which? so its researchers could try to book it.Booking.com's spokesperson added "a range of checks and verification measures" help secure the site, and technologies such as AI "help us detect and remove the majority of fraudulent listings within 24 hours".But Which? Travel editor Rory Boland said its checks had been shown to be "unfit for purpose"."If Booking.com's so-called sophisticated AI systems can't spot that 10 Downing Street is not a holiday rental, then it's no wonder scammers can exploit the platform so easily," he said."It would be laughable that we were able to list the UK's most famous address for rent, if the consequences weren't so devastating for holidaymakers, who risk losing thousands of pounds to bogus listings and phishing links."It is not the first time the site has faced criticism over its security efforts and customer service.'Prime city centre location'Which?'s listing, uploaded to Booking.com on 18 June, advertised a "1 bedroom apartment in the heart of London".It used images of the iconic 10 Downing Street front door, listed at its address - with a description referring to the one bedroom space as "a prime city centre location".Image source,Which?/Booking.comImage caption,A description for the property said it was 'situated on 10 Downing Street' and only a short walk of '400 metres' to Big BenIn the 20 minutes that Which? permitted customers to request a stay at its fake 10 Downing Street property, it said 14 people asked to do so.Only the booking request from a person known to be a Which? researcher was accepted.The watchdog's team also sent the researcher a message within Booking.com's system asking them to click an external link to confirm their payment details - something booking sites typically block to prevent customers being scammed.But Which? said that in this instance, Booking.com did not flag or remove the external link it sent.Booking.com said it had "visible reminders to not click on links customers are not confident about, and booking confirmations also provide further guidance, including details of the agreed payment schedule".The fake review left by Which? also seemingly passed the site's checks, despite bearing all the hallmarks of a joke."It was unbelievable that Booking.com let us stay at 10 Downing Street - the home of the UK PM!" it said.The listing itself was removed by the platform on 27 August.Image source,Which?/Booking.comImage caption,According to Which?, Booking.com said in a message the review would be checked by its moderators but it was added to the listing soon afterSome customers have previouslyaccused the firm of failing to protect them from falling victim to cyber-criminals."Fraud affects many industries, and 80% of UK adults believe scams are becoming more sophisticated," said Booking.com's spokesperson - adding it was continuing to strengthen its defencesin the face of this challenge.Which?, meanwhile, said more should be done to force booking sites to swiftly remove false listings under the Online Safety Act (OSA).The Act requires firms which have identified illegal content, including fraudulent material, on their sites to show they are committed to removing it.Boland said Ofcom, which enforces the OSA, should be encouraged use it to "crack down on irresponsible online platforms that leave consumers wide open to fraud"."For illegal content generated by users, platforms have existing legal duties that mean they must take it down swiftly once they become aware of it," an Ofcom spokesperson told Which?.Booking.com customers warned of 'reservation hijacking' after hackPublished15 AprilHolidaymaker loses â¬1,800 in phishing scamPublished14 October 2025Tourists descend on private home in Booking.com scamPublished3 August 2022Sign up for our Tech Decoded newsletterto follow the world's top tech stories and trends.Outside the UK? title: 贝森特表示，中国不同意G20反对“廉价出口”充斥市场的声明
content:
中国是唯一一个对一项联合声明持异议的二十国集团成员，该声明称“非市场经济体不断推出廉价出口是不可持续的”，财政部长斯科特·贝森特周二表示。

贝森特在与财长举行数日会议后的新闻发布会上表示，其他二十国集团成员将在未来“几天、几周或几个月”采取行动，“就这种不可持续的平衡达成一项决议”。财政部周二晚些时候发布的声明中包括一个脚注，明确指出中国反对其中 19 个成员国同意“各国应采取措施消除加剧失衡的非市场政策和做法”的一段话。

“特别是，拥有过度和持续外部盈余的国家应消除限制国内消费和导致过度依赖出口的扭曲。该段落写道。

美国财政部表示，中国还反对对霍尔木兹海峡的航运持续中断表示担忧的段落，霍尔木兹海峡是伊朗在与美国的战争中有效封锁的重要石油运输路线。

中国进一步反对赞扬国际货币基金组织“对全球失衡的监督”的段落，并特别指出“对二十国集团负有相当大一部分外债的国家”

中国美国大使馆没有立即回应 CNBC 就贝森特关于联合声明的言论发表评论的请求。

贝森特在新闻发布会上表示，“我本来希望能够在今天宣布一份一致的联合公报”，同时强调其他 19 名成员的协议“表明了中美关系的巨大性”。

此番言论发表之际，贝森特正在带头实施特朗普政府计划，通过二次制裁威胁伊朗的商业伙伴，从而扼杀伊朗经济，这一举措被称为“经济放逐行动”。

此举引发了人们的疑问，即美国是否会针对伊朗最大贸易伙伴及其最大石油买家中国。美国正在与北京进行长期贸易谈判，中国国家主席习近平定于 9 月下旬访问美国。

贝森特周二表示，“在伊朗问题上，我们的共同点多于分歧。”

“中国同意伊朗不能拥有核武器。中国同意霍尔木兹海峡必须有自由海上贸易。中国 50% 的能源来自海湾地区，”他

“因此，我认为中国有责任或有责任努力寻求解决方案，”贝森特补充道。 “我们将看看他们如何跟进。”

title: 自动驾驶飞机会改变天空吗？
content: Image source,PykaImage caption,Pyka's crop dusters are used in the US and BrazilByZoe CorbynTechnology Reporter,ÂReporting fromSan FranciscoPublished38 minutes agoOver an alfalfa field in California's San Joaquin Valley, a small crop-spraying plane is flying scarily low to the ground. There's little risk to humans though, as the plane is pilot-free."We can actually go lower than a human pilot can," says Russ Marotzke, as the aircraft skims over the crop.Flying lower means less spray drift and therefore less chemicals are needed than in conventional manned crop-dusting, he says.The pilotless plane belongs to Pyka, where Marotzke works as a flight test engineer.Based in a converted Second World War hangar overlooking San Francisco Bay, the start-up makes self-flying aircraft without cockpits, designed either to spray crops or deliver cargo.It is among a small group of companies racing to bring autonomous fixed-wing aircraft into commercial service.Flying urban air taxis, so called electric vertical take-off and landing (eVTOL) aircraft, have captured much of the attention around autonomous aviation.But a quieter race is also under way to deploy self-flying planes, first for jobs like crop spraying and cargo delivery â and eventually, many of their makers hope, carrying passengers too."A fully scaled, ubiquitous passenger operation is the holy grail," says Michael Norcia, Pyka's co-founder and CEO, who envisions a large fleet of minibus-capacity Pyka planes ferrying passengers up and down the US east and west coasts."There's a decent chance we'll get to that point before the eVTOL industry."I've come to one of Pyka's crop-sprayer test sites, about 80km (50 miles) east of the company's factory and reached by a bumpy dirt road.Today, Marotzke and a colleague are trying out a software update on a demonstration aircraft.About a dozen Pyka aircraft are already in Brazil where they are used to spray crops such as cotton and soybeans, work previously carried out by human pilots.The crop-spraying plane is fully electric, with its battery in the nose. It can fly for about 35 minutes and carries up to 300L of spray in a tank in its middle.Pyka's planes are sometimes called large drones, but it seems an understatement: they all have 11.5m wingspans.Inside a shipping container beside the field, the engineers highlight on a computer the area they want the aircraft to spray. The software then plans the route, taking account of obstacles such as nearby power lines that have already been mapped.The take-off, down a runway beside the field, is seamless. About 15 minutes later, after sensing that it is running low on spray â water for today's purposes â the aircraft lands itself for a manual refill and demonstration battery swap. It then takes to the air again to resume spraying precisely where it left off.Image source,Zoe CorbynImage caption,The batteries on Pyka drones last half an hourAutonomous flight is different from autopilot.Autopilot assists, much like cruise control and lane-keeping functions in a car.Autonomous systems aim to handle the entire flight, including take-off and landing, with little or no human intervention, using algorithms to process sensor data and control the aircraft.Self-flying planes have been slower to emerge than self-driving cars, despite operating in what is generally considered a more structured and predictable environment.That is partly because big tech companies "doubled down" on cars, pouring vast sums into the technology, says Mykel Kochenderfer, an expert in safe aviation autonomy at Stanford University.But it is also because aircraft are held to stricter safety standards than cars, creating a much higher bar for deployment."The consequences for air accidents can just be so severe," says Kochenderfer.Military interest has been helping propel the technology. Many of the companies have defence contracts to demonstrate and trial their systems, often with fewer regulatory hurdles than on the civilian side, and some are even alreadysupplying military customers,external.In the US, the largest autonomous fixed-wing aircraft approved for commercial civilian use so far is Pyka's crop sprayer, which won authorization last year.Though operations are limited to a tightly defined agricultural setting and require a ground operator and visual observer. It earlier secured similar approval in Brazil, where rules are more permissive.Pyka aims to scale up production from around two dozen planes a year currently to 1000 by 2030. Each sells for $550,000, with customers trained to operate them.Image source,WindracersImage caption,Windracers wants to launch an autonomous cargo serviceThe UK has yet to approve any such longer-term operations, though British firm Windracers is seeking permission to launch an autonomous cargo service in Shetland and Orkney. Its aircraft, designed to carry goods to remote areas, are also flying missions in Ukraine."It would be the first heavy-lift air cargo service by drone certainly in the UK and probably anywhere," says Stephen Wright, Windracers founder and chairman.Supporters say autonomous aircraft could address pilot shortages, remove people from dangerous work such as crop spraying, improve efficiency â for example, by allowing aircraft to carry more cargo â and cut costs if one operator can oversee many planes.They also argue automation could make flying safer, pointing to past declines in accidents as more automated systems have been introduced.Pilots' groups remain wary.The US Air Line Pilots Association (ALPA) calls removing pilots "a serious gamble with safety and a step too far".The US National Agricultural Aviation Association, which represents crop dusting pilots, says small uncrewed aircraft can be hard for its aviators to see. Piloted planes, it adds, can spray a much larger area faster.Image source,Reliable RoboticsImage caption,Reliable Robotics is retrofitting planes with its autonomous techPyka and Windracers are building aircraft from scratch, arguing this allows autonomy to be designed in from the outset and the aircraft tailored to the job.Others are retrofitting existing larger planes.Backed by Boeing's investment arm, US-based Reliable Robotics is currently testing its system on the Cessna 208B Grand Caravan, a single-pilot cargo plane that can carry about 1360kg of payload over hundreds of kilometers.Retrofitting on certified aircraft lets the company focus exclusively on proving the autonomous system's safety rather than also having to seek approval for a new aircraft, says Robert Rose, its co-founder and CEO.Merlin Labs, also US-based, has been working its way up through progressively larger military aircraft and is now applying its system to the two-pilot Lockheed Martin C-130J military transport plane, with commercial multi-crew cargo planes next."It is a common autonomy brain that can transition between different aircraft," explains Matt George, Merlin's founder and CEO.The companies also differ in their approach to AI.Reliable is avoiding it altogether, arguing it would complicate certification.Merlin, meanwhile, is taking a far more AI-centric approach.The divide is evident in so-called detect and avoid systems.One of autonomous flight's biggest challenges is replicating a pilot's ability to spot and maneuver safely around other aircraft and obstacles, and there is virtually no margin for error.With no perfect solution yet, companies are adding different sensor systems as well as duplicating those that already come as standard to provide extra back-up.Reliable has added forward-looking air-to-air radar to detect other aircraft more than eight kilometers ahead, with software that follows fixed rules to decide how the plane should respond.It is "better than a pilot's eyeballs" says Rose.Merlin, meanwhile, is using AI-powered cameras to detect and classify objects.Pyka has used lidar from the outset to detect trees, vehicles, large birds and terrain. But it's short range, so the company also plans to add AI-powered cameras, its first real use of AI onboard."For a lot of things there's no need to use AIâ¦but for figuring out that six pixels in the distance are an airplane versus some other smudge, it is perfect territory," says Norcia.The AI dilemma also extends to communicating with air traffic control.In shared airspace, aircraft must be able to receive, interpret and respond to radio instructions, typically from air traffic control.Reliable's solution is to have a remote pilot on the ground, initially fully trained, to handle communications and make safety-critical decisions.Merlin plans to use generative AI, trained on thousands of hours of recorded exchanges, to interpret instructions and respond itself."Our problem is harderâ¦ but we want to move beyond remote piloting," says George.Merlin plans to reduce pilots in stages, from two to one and eventually none.Pyka, says Norcia, is content to let others "blaze the trail" in finding the best way to operate in shared airspace.Meanwhile, even if fully autonomous passenger flight remains elusive, many expect the technology being pioneered will inch into commercial aviation, potentially making piloted flying safer.That, notes ALPA, the US pilots' association, would be a welcome development.Related topicsInternational BusinessTechnology of BusinessArtificial intelligence

title: 帕洛阿尔托首席执行官表示 1 万亿美元的网络安全基础设施尚未为人工智能做好准备
content:
Palo Alto Networks 首席执行官 Nikesh Arora 周二表示，人工智能正在迫使企业彻底检修大约 1 万亿美元的老化网络安全基础设施，这些基础设施是为人工智能出现之前的世界而构建的。

“七十年前部署的任何设备都没有准备好以机器速度处理人工智能，”Arora 在 CNBC 的 Jim Cramer 节目“Mad Money”中表示。 “你必须重新考虑你的网络架构。”

帕洛阿尔托周二的盈利报告表明，紧迫性已经转化为业务。该公司超出了第四财季的预期，并发布了新财年的强劲前景。 Cramer's Charitable Trust 是 CNBC 投资俱乐部运营的投资组合，拥有 Palo Alto 和网络同行 CrowdStrike。

Arora 预计机会会不断增长，因为人工智能使攻击者能够比以往更快地发现和利用漏洞，迫使公司对并非针对自动威胁而设计的安全防御进行现代化改造。他说：“如果没有做好网络安全，就无法成功部署人工智能。”

“全球约有 1 万亿美元的网络安全债务必须进行现代化改造，以抵御自动化威胁，因为它们是即时运行的。”

这一机会标志着投资者与今年早些时候对人工智能对网络安全影响的看法发生了巨大逆转。由于担心功能日益强大的人工智能模型可能会破坏传统安全软件，帕洛阿尔托和其他网络安全股票面临压力。最终，市场开始将人工智能视为增长动力，因为投资者认识到攻击者可以将同一技术武器化。

“九个月前，……我们有罪并被判濒临死亡，因为人工智能将吃掉我们的午餐、早餐和晚餐，”阿罗拉告诉克莱默。 “看来事实并非如此。看来我们得和他们一起吃盛宴了。”

Arora 指出今年早些时候 Anthropic 的 Mythos 模型的出现是一个转折点。神话促使公司更加认真地对待网络安全，因为该模型可以很容易地用于利用软件漏洞。自 4 月 7 日以来，Palo Alto 的股价已飙升 113%。在此之前，该股在 2026 年一直处于亏损状态。

“八年来，我一直在努力告诉客户他们还没有准备好，而 [Anthropic 首席执行官 Dario Amodei] 在一次活动中就做到了，仅仅通过推出 Mythos，”Arora 在 CNBC 上表示。

Arora 表示 Palo Alto 已与大约向 2,000 家公司介绍其前沿人工智能关键防御计划，该计划使用先进的人工智能模型来测试客户的防御、识别漏洞并帮助他们实现安全基础设施的现代化。该公司于 8 月正式推出了该计划。

虽然 Arora 警告称，这笔支出不会立即全部实现，但他表示人工智能从根本上扩大了网络安全行业机会的规模和持续时间。

“并不是所有事情都会在下个季度发生，”Arora 告诉 Cramer。 “但我要说的是，这不仅改变了帕洛阿尔托，而且改变了整个行业的网络安全的长期增长率和持续时间。”

title: Palo Alto Networks 人工智能需求超出季度预期，继续大举收购
content:
由于人工智能风险不断增加，对其网络安全工具的需求增加，Palo Alto Networks 的第四季度业绩超出了预期。

股价在常规交易时段下跌 5% 后，在盘后交易中下跌了约 2%。

该公司的业绩与 LSEG 的预期相比如下：

该季度收入从一年前的 25.4 亿美元跃升了 34%该公司表示，之前。 Palo Alto 报告净亏损 2.82 亿美元，即每股 35 美分，低于一年前的净利润 2.54 亿美元，即每股 36 美分。

首席执行官 Nikesh Arora 告诉 CNBC，人工智能攻击的加速迫使客户建立更好、更快的网络防御。这些担忧已经起到了推动作用，但长期增长仍处于早期阶段。

“这是一个长期的顺风车，”他说。 “这不会在一个季度内发生，也不会在两个季度内发生。从增长率的角度来看，它只是支撑了我们业务的长期持续时间。”

随着像 Anthropic 的 Mythosspurs 这样的高性能人工智能模型的兴起，Palo Alto Networks 的股价今年几乎翻了一番，需要更新的安全工具来检测和响应代理网络攻击。

代理人工智能问题随着违规行为而加速，例如theOpenAI-Hugging Facehack，证明代理可以越来越多地自主计划和编排攻击。

但帕洛阿尔托并不是人工智能安全竞赛的唯一受益者。上周，随着客户购买更多网络工具，CrowdStrike 和 Oktasurgedon 都对盈利和指引表示乐观。

Arora 表示，在 AnthropicMythos 推出后，Palo Alto 已举办了 2,000 多场客户简报会，高于上季度披露的约 1,200 场。

Palo Alto 还宣布收购 AI 初创公司 Console，以深化其 AI 安全产品。在短短一年多的时间里，Arora 加速了积极的交易推动，其中包括斥资 250 亿美元收购身份安全公司 CyberArk，斥资近 34 亿美元收购 Chronosphere，这是该公司迄今为止最大的一笔收购。

Arora 表示：“我将网络创业生态系统视为一个大型实验室，人们在其中尝试不同的事物。”Arora 补充道，如果 Palo 的内部方法不起作用，它可以寻求从该领域进行收购。

Palo Alto 表示乐观。预计第一季度收入为 33.0 亿美元至 33.1 亿美元，高于分析师预测的 32.2 亿美元。

对于全年，该公司预测收入在 141 亿美元至 142 亿美元之间，调整后每股收益为 4.16 美元至 4.19 美元。这超出了 137.9 亿美元的收入和 4.11 美元的每股收益预期。

title: 戴尔上调 2027 财年 AI 服务器实力预测后股价飙升 9%
content:
戴尔科技公司公布的业绩和预测轻松超出了华尔街的预期，周二盘后交易中该公司股价上涨 9%。

该公司相对于 LSEG 共识的表现如下：

根据一份声明，截至 7 月 31 日的第二财季收入高于所有预期，同比增长约 58%。净利润为 41.3 亿美元，即每股 6.34 美元，高于去年同期的 11.6 亿美元，即每股 1.70 美元。调整后收益排除了股票薪酬的影响。

对于第三财季，戴尔预计营收为 490 亿美元，调整后每股收益为 6.50 美元，这意味着增长 81%。伦敦证券交易所集团 (LSEG) 调查的分析师预计每股收益为 4.49 美元，营收为 414.2 亿美元。

戴尔上调了全年预期。该公司目前预计调整后每股收益为 25.50 美元，收入为 1,920 亿美元。接受 LSEG 调查的分析师预计每股收益为 18.92 美元，收入为 1726.7 亿美元。截至 5 月，该公司 2027 年指导方针包括调整后每股收益 17.90 美元，收入为 1650 亿至 1690 亿美元。

戴尔运营主管杰夫·克拉克 (Jeff Clarke) 在与公司的电话会议上表示，投入成本攀升导致的价格上涨是收入指导方针提高的一个因素。截至周二收盘，戴尔股价今年迄今已上涨 236%，而同期标准普尔 500 指数上涨 11%。该股票已成为希望押注人工智能基础设施持续增长的投资者的热门选择。 7月份，特朗普总统自去年重返办公室以来一直购买戴尔股票，他再次推荐购买戴尔电脑。

根据彭博社的计算，该公司创始人、董事长兼首席执行官迈克尔·戴尔(Michael Dell)现在是全球第五大富豪。

“德克萨斯州有一句老话，我可能刚刚编造出来……”，结果公布后，迈克尔·戴尔在 X 上发帖称。 “如果你的每股收益保持同比 200% 以上的增长，就会有好事发生。”

该公司针对数据中心硬件的基础设施解决方案集团公布的第二财季收入为 317.8 亿美元，增长 89%，高于 StreetAccount 调查的分析师普遍预期的 296.1 亿美元。在该领域，戴尔通过人工智能优化的服务器创造了 164 亿美元的收入。这一数字高于 StreetAccount 160.7 亿美元的共识。

存储收入为 48.5 亿美元，增长了近 26%。来自传统服务器和网络设备的收入猛增 122%，达到 105.3 亿美元。

“我们看到，越来越多的客户需要有意义的 CPU 计算能力来支持 AI 和代理工作流程，”Clarke 说。 “这些工作负载正在增加对传统服务器的需求。”

戴尔的客户端解决方案集团向消费者和商业客户销售个人电脑和配件，贡献了 150.3 亿美元的收入。该数字增长了 20%，但略低于 StreetAccount 150.8 亿美元的共识。

“我们今年早些时候所做的事情之一是我们看到 PC 市场在下半年出现疲软迹象，”Clarke 说。 “我们优化了基础设施业务的比特和字节。”

本季度，戴尔获得了一份价值 97 亿美元的合同，为美国军方提供软件，而以人工智能为中心的云基础设施提供商 Iren 表示，它同意购买价值 16 亿美元的戴尔硬件，包括包含 Nvidia 芯片的服务器。

戴尔目前预计本财年人工智能优化服务器销售额将达到 740 亿美元，将增长 200%。就在六个月前，该公司还预测增长 103%。

title: GoPro 加入人工智能热潮，进军数据中心，股价飙升 40%
content:
GoPro 加入人工智能热潮。

根据一份新闻稿，这家运动相机制造商周二宣布，将与私营光子公司 Starman Optical 进行最终合并，并进军人工智能数据中心和国防市场。

“我们预计此次合并将使 GoPro 作为美国领先的成像和光学解决方案公司，在消费、商业和国防市场上实现增长，解决与相机、光学和人工智能相关的国家安全重要领域GoPro 首席执行官尼古拉斯·伍德曼 (Nicholas Woodman) 在新闻稿中表示。

消息传出后，股价收盘上涨 40%。 GoPro 拒绝透露有关此举的更多细节。

作为交易的一部分，该公司股东将获得 2.85 亿美元现金，即每股 1.14 美元，并且该股票将继续在纳斯达克上市。

从这一消息中受益最大的股东之一是 Youtuber Markiplier，根据 7 月 13 日提交的文件，他收购了 8.5% 的巨额股份。私募股权公司贝莱德今年夏天早些时候也披露了 6.4% 的股份。

自 2014 年以每股 38 美元的价格上市以来，GoPro 多年来一直在努力赢得投资者的信心，直到几天前，其交易价格仍处于低价股水平。

该公司还表示，其 9200 万美元的债务将在交易完成时偿还，并且“将继续全力支持其现有的消费产品及其订阅和订阅服务”。云平台，同时投资于增长和更广泛、多元化的产品路线图。”

GoPro 并不是唯一关注人工智能热潮的知名消费者品牌。

4 月份，苦苦挣扎的零售商 Allbird 宣布，它将从生产可持续鞋转向人工智能计算和硬件，将自己重新命名为 Smartbird。

“当人们遇到不理解的事情时，他们总是翻白眼，”Smartbird 首席执行官纳迪亚·卡尔斯滕 (Nadia Carlsten) 在接受采访时表示上周在 CNBC 的“The Exchange”节目中。

“这是关于开发产品、建立客户渠道、确保全世界了解您正在开发的产品、让客户签署合同以实际向他们销售您的产品等等，”她补充道。

title: OpenAI 表示 Astra 人工智能模型是第一个跨越“关键”网络安全能力的模型
content:
OpenAIon 周二表示，其即将推出的人工智能模型 Astra 是第一个跨越其“关键”网络安全能力门槛的产品。

该公司表示，Astra 可以发现以前未知的安全漏洞并在没有人类逐步指导的情况下利用它们，这意味着该模型属于其所谓的准备框架的最高级类别。 OpenAI 表示，仍计划“很快”推出 Astra，但对其网络安全功能的访问将更加有限。

OpenAI 于 2023 年推出了其准备框架，它是该公司“跟踪和准备可能带来新的严重危害风险的先进人工智能功能”的方法。在去年对该框架的更新中，该公司概述了“高”能力阈值，其中模型可以放大导致严重伤害的“现有路径”，以及“关键”能力阈值，其中模型可能引入“前所未有的新路径”以造成严重伤害。

“我们将在发布时在模型的系统卡中分享有关我们的安全、安保和一致性测试和评估的更多详细信息，”OpenAI 在博客文章中表示。周二。

OpenAI 上个月披露其两个模型逃离了训练环境、访问了开放网络并破坏了 Hugging Face 的系统，该公司的安全实践受到了严格审查。 OpenAI 将此次攻击定性为“前所未有的网络事件”，并暂时暂停了部分内部训练和研究。

该公司决定推迟 Astra 的部分开发，尽管该模型并未参与 Hugging Face 事件。在加强和测试保护后，OpenAI 周二表示，它相信该模型的保障措施“足以最大限度地降低在我们的准备框架下发布时造成严重损害的风险。”

OpenAI 表示，Astra 的先进网络功能将可供其网络安全联盟 Daybreak 中的一组精选组织使用。
